subject: Draft: GPU on-ramp and minimum commit options for Solaris Bio
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Nina Park <nina@solarisbio.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU on-ramp and minimum commit options for Solaris Bio

Hi Nina — great talking earlier. As discussed, here's what I'd like to capture to put together a short reservation proposal:

- Target go-live date and ramp milestones (e.g., internal beta, external launch).
- Expected steady-state concurrent QPS / peak QPS and average tokens per request.
- Latency SLO (p50/p95) and any critical endpoints that need reserved capacity.
- Any data residency or private deployment constraints.

If you can fill the attached capacity_questionnaire.docx and send a recent traffic_sample.csv we can size a few reservation options (min GPUs, cluster sizing, and a 4/8/12-week ramp schedule) and include pricing bands for committed vs on-demand overage.

Thanks — I'll draft three options (conservative / standard / accelerated) once we have the numbers.

— Lauren Bishop

lauren@redwood.com

Hi Lauren — thanks, attaching a short traffic sample and our answers inline.

Quick context: Solaris is planning to embed a clinical note summarization assistant into our provider portal. Goal for phase 1 is internal pilots in August, public beta in September.

- Expected average request size: ~800 tokens in, ~300 tokens out
- Expected steady-state QPS (phase 1): 8 qps; projected peak QPS at launch: 35 qps for short bursts
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for text generation endpoints
- Data residency: US-only; SOC2 evidence available on request

Attached: traffic_sample.csv (sampling of request counts by hour). Procurement is looped for contract/timing.

Best,
Nina

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 14:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: GPU on-ramp and minimum commit options for Solaris Bio (internal)

Team — Nina sent the traffic_sample and timeline. They want internal pilots in August, public beta in September. Key constraints: p95 < 300ms, US-only, initial peak ~35 qps.

Draft sizing assumptions I used:
- We should price for both LLM serving and KV cache headroom. Assume 40% request burstiness and 25% sustained batching efficiency.
- Baseline perf target: gpt-like family running with quantized 16-bit profile => ~1.2 qps per A100x GPU at their prompt lengths (conservative); with better batching/kv caching could hit ~2.0 qps.

Options to include in the proposal (spread sheet SOL-commitment-options-v1.xlsx attached):
1) Flex Starter — minimal commitment, small cluster: 16 min GPUs, 4-week on-ramp to 48 GPUs; best for small pilot, higher overage unit cost.
2) Standard Ramp — balanced: 32 min GPUs, 8-week ramp to 96 GPUs; recommended for predictable beta + initial production.
3) FastLane Commit — 64 min GPUs, 12-week ramp to 160 GPUs with burst pool and reserved backup capacity; recommended if they want low-latency and heavy parallel workloads at launch.

Costing: provide committed GPU-hour rate + overage rate per option; include an option for 12-month term discount vs 3-month pilot. Also provide optional Dedicated private VPC deployment add-on pricing (SOC2 supporting docs available).

Action items: Marcus to add runway numbers for caching effects and Monica to draft the SLA and onboarding timeline. Aditya — can you run a quick sensitivity on per-token unit economics for each option? I want the proposal PDF by Tuesday EOD.

— Lauren

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Nina Park <nina@solarisbio.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver@solarisbio.com>, Procurement <procurement@solarisbio.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Tiered reservation + on-ramp options for Solaris Bio (preview)

Hi Nina / Oliver — attaching a short proposal PDF that lays out three reservation paths. Summary below; full numbers in SOL-proposal-tiered-onramp.pdf.

Executive summary: based on your sample traffic and target p95, we recommend Option 2 (Standard Ramp) as the sweet spot for beta -> launch while balancing committed spend and latency SLOs. We include a FastLane Commit for lower latency and larger burst capacity if Solaris prefers an aggressive go-live.

Option A — Flex Starter (pilot friendly)
- Minimum reservation: 16 GPUs
- Typical ramp: 4 weeks to 48 GPUs (weekly linear increases)
- Use case: internal pilot / limited user group
- Committed term: 3 months (auto-convert to month-to-month)
- Estimated committed monthly cost: $48,000 (committed rate) + overage $0.45 / GPU-hour

Option B — Standard Ramp (recommended)
- Minimum reservation: 32 GPUs
- Typical ramp: 8 weeks to 96 GPUs (front-loaded first 3 weeks)
- Use case: beta -> production with predictable traffic
- Committed term: 6 or 12 months
- Estimated committed monthly cost: $86,400 (committed rate) + overage $0.35 / GPU-hour

Option C — FastLane Commit (accelerated, low-latency)
- Minimum reservation: 64 GPUs
- Typical ramp: 12 weeks to 160 GPUs (includes 20% burst pool)
- Use case: production at scale with strict p95 SLOs and high concurrency
- Committed term: 12 months recommended
- Estimated committed monthly cost: $156,000 (committed rate) + overage $0.25 / GPU-hour

Additional notes:
- Each option includes autoscaling policies, KV/prefix caching recommendations, and a suggested quantization profile.
- We will reserve a 5% buffer cluster for scheduled maintenance and can auto-fallback to hosted models in a different region if required.
- SOC2 summary and onboarding checklist attached (SOC2-summary.pdf).

Next steps: 1) Confirm preferred option and term length; 2) Procurement to confirm PO timeline; 3) We issue a DocuSign SOW and set an onboarding kickoff (2 weeks prep).

Attachment: SOL-proposal-tiered-onramp.pdf (pdf)

Warmly,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
